content.user_title: Choose the Right AI Tool for Every Task
content.value_statement: Choosing between many skills and agents can delay technical work. This skill maps each task to focused tools using concise catalogs and selection rules.
actual_capabilities: Distinguishes lightweight reference skills from agents designed for reasoning and decisions.
Maps common development tasks to named skills using trigger phrases.
Recommends agents for exploration, planning, scraping, Git work, and project organization.
Provides catalogs covering languages, frameworks, infrastructure, data tools, and file formats.
Limits recommendations to two or three tools for a focused response.
limitations: Recommendations depend on the catalogs included with the skill.
The skill does not verify that a recommended tool is installed.
The skill does not execute recommended tools or complete the underlying task.
Catalog entries may become outdated when available skills or agents change.

use_cases.title: Route a development question
use_cases.description: Identify the most relevant skill for a language, framework, database, or infrastructure question.

use_cases.title: Select an investigation agent
use_cases.description: Choose an agent for codebase exploration, architecture planning, web extraction, or project organization.

use_cases.title: Find a file processing tool
use_cases.description: Compare libraries and command-line tools for documents, archives, media, and structured data.

prompt_templates.title: Choose one tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Which skill or agent should I use for [task]? Recommend one primary option and explain the match.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a direct recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare possible tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the best tools for [task]. Recommend no more than three options and explain when each option fits.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user sees several plausible choices.

prompt_templates.title: Route a multi-part task
prompt_templates.prompt: Break [project] into major task types. Match each task to a skill or agent and identify the recommended order.
prompt_templates.scenario: A project requires several specialized tools.

prompt_templates.title: Design an efficient tool strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tool strategy for [complex goal] with [constraints]. Prefer skills for reference work and agents for decisions.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs coordinated routing under constraints.

output_examples.input: Which tool should I use to find where a function is defined?
output_examples.output: Use the file-search skill first for a focused lookup. Use the Explore agent only when the question requires broader codebase investigation.

output_examples.input: I need to plan a React feature and then implement its state logic.
output: Use the Plan agent to define the implementation approach.
Use react-ops for React patterns and state guidance.

output_examples.input: What should I use to inspect a CSV file?
output_examples.output: Use pandas for analysis or the csv module for streaming. Use csvkit when a command-line workflow is more suitable.

best_practices: Describe the task, desired result, and important constraints.
Use a focused skill before selecting a broader agent for simple lookups.
Confirm that recommended tools are available before depending on them.
anti_patterns: Do not request many tools when one focused option can complete the task.
Do not assume a catalog recommendation installs or runs the named tool.
Do not use an agent for a simple reference question without a clear need.

faq.question: What does this skill recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends skills for focused reference work and agents for tasks requiring broader reasoning or decisions.

faq.question: Does it install recommended tools?
faq.answer: No. It only provides recommendations and reference information.

faq.question: Can it complete the selected task?
faq.answer: No. The selected skill or agent must handle the actual task.

faq.question: How many tools will it recommend?
faq.answer: It generally recommends no more than two or three relevant tools.

faq.question: Which technical areas are covered?
faq.answer: Coverage includes languages, frameworks, databases, infrastructure, file formats, data processing, and development workflows.

faq.question: Can recommendations become outdated?
faq.answer: Yes. Recommendations reflect the included catalogs and may not include newly added or renamed tools.
